lines.text: A humanoid robot just clocked in for a full eight-hour factory shift.
On November 4th, Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun shared a video from the final assembly workshop of Xiaomi's electric car factory.
The job: sorting side covers for the car's centre console. Xiaomi says its robots kept going for 8 hours and 5 minutes.
In the sped-up video, they pause to recharge twice: after about 3 hours, and again after about 6.
When one robot dropped a part on the floor, a wheeled robot rolled over and picked it up.
Earlier this year, a Xiaomi humanoid did a factory internship. Now it's working full shifts.
The catch: Xiaomi hasn't said how often humans had to step in. But robots on real car lines are getting closer.
